scope: Also covers how such policies and their perception modules are trained in simulation and carried to real robots (sim-to-real transfer, domain randomization) and the simulated grasp datasets they learn from; simulator engineering itself stays out.

concepts.title: Sim-to-real transfer
concepts.definition: Deploying a policy or perception model trained in simulation on a physical robot, which works only insofar as the model survives the gap between simulated and real dynamics, sensing and appearance.

near_pairs.name: Reality gap
near_pairs.why: Tobin2017domain suggests it separately; claims use 'sim-to-real gap' for the discrepancy that this transfer must bridge. Here it is folded in, but it could stand as its own phenomenon.

near_pairs.name: Domain randomization
near_pairs.why: A technique for achieving sim-to-real transfer, drafted as a separate extra concept; not the same thing.

concepts.title: ACRONYM dataset
concepts.definition: A large simulated grasp dataset of ShapeNet object meshes, each with many physics-checked parallel-jaw grasps, that is widely used to train and evaluate 6-DoF grasp generators.

concepts.title: Domain randomization
concepts.definition: Training on many simulated environments with randomized textures, lighting, camera, geometry or dynamics, so that the real world looks like just another variation and a model trained only in simulation transfers.

near_pairs.name: Synthetic training data for 6D pose estimation
near_pairs.why: Existing concept; randomized synthetic images are one kind of synthetic training data, but domain randomization also covers dynamics and policy training.
